metas.name: Canola
metas.note: Canola is a low-growing crop with yellow flowers that is used to make cooking oil. It is usually planted during the off-season for rice, making it extremely common north of Padma river in the state of Dhaka.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bangladesh.

metas.name: Corn
metas.note:
Corn tends to be planted in the west of Bangladesh - large and medium-sized fields can be found in Rajshahi, Rangpur, western Mymensingh and northern Khulna.

Smaller patches of corn can be found in the south of Barishal, usually adjacent to other crops.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bangladesh.

metas.name: early growth rice
metas.note:
Rice is the main agricultural crop in Bangladesh and is planted twice a year. The different rice seasons can be told apart by the height and colour of the rice and are very useful for regionguessing.

Short green rice that is barely sticking out of the water is known as early growth rice. Early growth rice can be seen in the states of Khulna, Mymensingh and south of Padma River in Dhaka.

metas.name: east-west ridge hazy
metas.note: A sizable east-west ridge can be seen on the Indian border from the northern parts of Sylhet and eastern Mymensingh. It is often obscured or diminished by heavy haze.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bangladesh.

metas.name: fruit trees
metas.note: Standalone fruit trees in Bangladesh are most commonly seen in the states of Rajshahi and Rangpur. Fruit orchards with systematically planted trees, however, are concentrated near the Indian border in both states.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bangladesh.

metas.name: Fully-grown rice
metas.note:
Fully-grown rice is characterised by being noticeably taller, as well as having a yellow or orange colour and fluffier tips - the fluffiness signifies that the rice is ripe. Fully-grown rice is mostly seen in the state of Rajshahi, but it is also present in Rangpur and Chittagong.

metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bangladesh.

metas.name: Harvested rice
metas.note:
Harvested rice can be identified by its beige or brown colour and shorter, cut down appearance. It can be seen alongside fully-grown, unharvested rice as well as freshly planted early growth rice in adjacent fields. This is most commonly seen in the states of Sylhet and southern Khulna.

metas.name: hills
metas.note: While most of Bangladesh is almost completely flat, in the eastern parts of Chittagong you may find fairly tall, forested and uncultivated hills.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bangladesh.

metas.name: hip roofs
metas.note:
Bangladesh has several distinct roof styles that create an east/west divide in the country.

The west, particularly the divisions of Rajshahi, Khulna and Dhaka, is dominated by hip roofs made of sheet metal. The states of Rangpur and Chittagong tend to have mixed roofs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bangladesh.

metas.name: Jute
metas.note: Jute is a tall-growing green crop which gets dried and used in the making of rugs, bags and other goods. Because of when the coverage was taken, jute can almost exclusively be found on Street View in Rangpur. In its dried state it can be found hanging off fences and drying on the roads anywhere in the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bangladesh.

metas.name: rice middle of growing
metas.note:
Slightly taller rice, in the middle of growing, which still remains green, can be seen in the states of Rangpur, Barishal and Chittagong.

metas.name: Shitcam
metas.note: Shitcam coverage is only found in and around Dhaka.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bangladesh.

metas.name: Sunflower fields
metas.note: Sunflower fields are found in the south of Barishal state.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bangladesh.

metas.name: Tea
metas.note: Tea production in Bangladesh is concentrated in the highlands of southern Sylhet and, rarely, Chittagong.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bangladesh.

metas.name: Tiled roofs
metas.note: Tiled roofs are uncommon in Bangladesh, but the ones you do see are of West Bengal origin, and are thus only found on the Indian border in the state of Khulna.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bangladesh.

metas.name: triangular "window"
metas.note: In the east, you will commonly see sheet metal roofs with a triangular "window" just below the ridge of the roof. The state of Sylhet will exclusively have this style, which can also be seen in Chittagong, Mymensingh, eastern Rangpur and northern Dhaka.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bangladesh.

metas.name: Vast rice fields
metas.note: Vast rice fields with almost nothing else in view can be seen in the border area between the states of Dhaka, Mymensingh and Sylhet.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bangladesh.

metas.name: Watermelons
metas.note: Fields of watermelons can also be found in the south of Barishal.
